title: ZZ-Free bSWAP Gates under Strong Driving in Far-Detuned Fixed-Frequency Transmons
summary: Far-detuned frequency allocations in fixed-frequency superconducting processors mitigate spectral crowding but constrain cross-resonance interactions at practical drive amplitudes. Here, we demonstrate that a single strong drive induces a large $XX-YY$ interaction in the far-detuned regime, while a weak second tone tunes the accompanying $ZZ$ phase. The interaction realizes a 150-ns $\sqrt{\mathrm{bSWAP}}$ gate, which can directly prepare a maximally entangled state from the ground state.
